papers.title: Agentic Game Development as a Verifiable Trajectory Data Engine for Scaling World Models

summary.tldr: A new post-training framework, Reinforcement Learning with Human-Engine Verification (RLHEV), uses game development code and engine runtimes as verifiable trajectory data engines for spatial world models.
key_points: Identifies game development code as an executable world specification capable of providing grounded spatial rewards via engine-based physics, collision, navigability, and playability checks.
Proposes Reinforcement Learning with Human-Engine Verification (RLHEV) to replace fuzzy spatial proxies like CLIP scores with dense engine signals combined with human developer acceptance feedback.
Leverages the game development process to generate real-world, long-horizon trajectory data suitable for RL post-training of world models.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes an executable, verifiable data engine for spatial world models, enabling effective RL post-training similar to compiler-based feedback loops in code agents.

papers.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?

summary.tldr: PAWBench and its evaluation protocol PAWEval benchmark video generation models as stochastic world models to measure how accurately repeated rollouts capture the real-world probability distribution of multi-outcome physical behaviors.
key_points: Formalizes probabilistic alignment as a distributional criterion requiring world models to generate the correct distribution of valid outcomes under identical initial conditions.
Introduces PAWBench, comprising 50 distinct physical scenarios, to evaluate whether video models act as accurate stochastic samplers.
Presents PAWEval, an outcome-level protocol that translates multiple generated video rollouts into empirical outcome distributions.
Evaluates eleven current video generation systems and finds that none consistently match reference probabilities while maintaining the full range of valid physical behaviors.
summary.why_it_matters: Determining whether video models achieve probabilistic alignment reveals whether they function as true physical world models rather than just generators of single plausible visual trajectories.

papers.title: UrbanGround: From Local Perception to Spatial Agency in a Real-Scale City

summary.tldr: UrbanGround is the first 3D sandbox built from territory-wide geospatial data of Hong Kong to evaluate MLLM agents' ability to translate first-person visual perception into navigation and spatial reasoning.
key_points: Replicates a real-scale city (Hong Kong) using territory-wide 3D geospatial data to support first-person, closed-loop navigation and interactive map usage.
Evaluates MLLMs across three dimensions: local scene grounding after active observation, navigation to distant/implicit goals, and robustness to changing route availability and pedestrian motion.
Identifies key agent failures in orientation, pedestrian-aware movement, and error accumulation during extended exploration where local perception fails to compose into goal-directed behavior.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a realistic, physically constrained benchmark to identify why current MLLMs fail at long-horizon spatial agency and navigation in real-world urban environments.

papers.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: Test-Time Policy Optimization (TTPO) introduces an asymmetric objective combining On-Policy Self-Distillation and Grouped RL with token-level selection, enabling label-free test-time training for mathematical reasoning in large language models.
key_points: TTPO addresses majority-vote pseudo-label fragility by treating agreeing and disagreeing rollouts asymmetrically.
Agreeing rollouts are distilled via On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) while down-weighting already-converged token positions.
Disagreeing rollouts are penalized using Grouped RL, restricting penalties to confident token-level errors.
Majority-vote routing strengthens self-supervision as model quality improves, matching label-supervised OPSD across five competition-level benchmarks.
Evaluations show Qwen3-1.7B performance increased from 38.0% to 45.2% during test-time training, with non-thinking gains between +25.2% and +36.4%.
summary.why_it_matters: TTPO enables large language models to continuously improve their mathematical reasoning performance at test time without relying on ground-truth labels.

papers.title: Self-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Flow Matching Models without Teacher

summary.tldr: Self-OPD is a teacher-free on-policy distillation framework for flow matching models that replaces external teachers with self-exploration, SDE trajectory branching, and advantage-weighted pull-push optimization.
key_points: Branches deterministic next-state predictions into K stochastic SDE candidates at each timestep, rolling them out via ODE samplers.
Calculates normalized advantages by comparing candidate rewards against a deterministic self-reference baseline.
Optimizes the velocity field using an all-branch pull-push objective featuring direction-aware attenuation and SDE-variance normalization.
Handles multi-objective alignment by fusing normalized scores directly at the reward level to prevent gradient conflicts.
summary.why_it_matters: It removes the high computational cost of training task-specific teacher models and mitigates compounding trajectory errors in flow matching distillation.

papers.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: A new framework formalizes agentic data as a factorized tuple (E,q,τ,v) and evaluates generation strategies using the Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity (ACE) lens.
key_points: Defines agentic data as a factorized object containing four core components: environment specification (E), task signal (q), interaction realization (τ), and optional verifier (v).
Introduces the ACE lens (Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity) to formulate agentic data generation as constrained distribution design.
Accuracy defines the feasible support of grounded, consistent data; Complexity aligns difficulty relative to a specific learner's capabilities; divErsity manages coverage and redundancy.
Highlights a literature shift toward execution-grounded verification, learner-calibrated difficulty, and behavioral coverage over raw dataset scaling.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces ad-hoc data generation with a structured theoretical framework for synthesizing valid, appropriately challenging, and non-redundant training data for LLM agents.

papers.title: Training Agents to Evolve with Their Harness: TaoLive Digital Avatar Agent Technical Report

summary.tldr: Harness-Aware Training (HAT) enables compact LLMs to adapt to evolving digital avatar agent harnesses without retraining model weights or degrading baseline generalization performance.
key_points: Harness-State Augmentation (HSA) applies task-preserving transformations to Skill identifiers, tool schemas, prompt structures, and Hook functions.
Training uses a three-stage pipeline: HSA-SFT on strong-model trajectories, General On-Policy Distillation to recover baseline generalization, and HSA-RL for robustness.
HAT achieves 94.8 on Live-Stream QA and 94.6 on Harness-Variant QA while raising IFEval score to 83.5, avoiding the 7.7-point regression caused by Fixed-Harness SFT.
Deployed on one NVIDIA H20 GPU, the system achieves P50 and P95 latencies of 3.4s and 8.1s in Taobao Live's digital-avatar production service.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows lightweight models to achieve low-latency execution and high accuracy in production live-streaming environments while seamlessly adapting to frequent tool and prompt updates.

papers.title: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games

summary.tldr: GameWAM is the first World-Action Model for native closed-loop gameplay and GUI control, unifying visual prediction and keyboard-mouse action generation via parallel flow matching.
key_points: Uses parallel visual and action generative processes with block-causal conditioning and flow matching to jointly generate visual futures and action trajectories.
Handles heterogeneous native control by predicting a gameplay/GUI mode per step, employing mode-specific prediction distributions and continuous-action normalization.
Implements block-cycle control for long-horizon planning by predicting beyond a committed horizon, executing a short action prefix, and replanning using hierarchical cross-cycle history.
Identifies Low-Frequency Action Source Imprinting (LASI), a failure mode where low-frequency components of the sampled action source steer coarse generated camera motion.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that unifying world modeling and action generation enables higher task success in complex video games using fewer executed native inputs.

papers.title: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents

summary.tldr: PILOT introduces a supervisor-worker agent harness for live self-improvement, using mid-run steering and real-time self-evolution to refine active trajectories and store persistent skills.
key_points: Couples live steering (allowing a supervisor to interrupt, redirect, or abort active workers) with live self-evolution (distilling failure modes into persistent skills and memory).
Outperforms existing counterpart harnesses on Terminal-Bench 2.0 by up to 9.8 percentage points.
Improves self-improvement task performance by 14.6 points using GLM-5.1 and 12.4 points using Kimi-K2.6.
Reduces mean output tokens by up to 47.4% while increasing successful evaluations per million output tokens by up to 134.0%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables AI agents to fix trajectory errors in real time while significantly reducing token consumption and improving execution efficiency during complex, long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization

summary.tldr: Zero-WAM is a causal video-action model that achieves zero-shot cross-task robot manipulation by following in-context human video prompts without parameter updates.
key_points: Uses HumanGen, an automated dataset containing 74.2K human-robot in-context learning pairs across 8.6K tasks converted from task-sampled robot trajectories.
Employs an in-context future chunk prediction (IFP) training objective to suppress task-shortcut learning and force reliance on the human video prompt.
Achieved a 47.0% average success rate across seven unseen RoboTwin 2.0 simulation tasks, outperforming the top video-action baseline by 29.5 percentage points.
Demonstrated real-world generalization to unseen task configurations including multi-object scenes, long-horizon tasks, and fine-grained insertions.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robots to generalize to entirely unseen manipulation tasks by directly using unlabeled human demonstration videos as context prompts rather than requiring explicit re-training or fine-tuning.

papers.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO

summary.tldr: A systematic study demonstrates that Evolution Strategies (ES) achieve broader reasoning coverage and higher Pass@K performance than GRPO by maintaining population diversity and avoiding entropy collapse during post-training.
key_points: Evolution Strategies (ES) prevent entropy collapse, resulting in superior Pass@K performance compared to Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Verifier-projected Jensen-Shannon diversity across the ES population theoretically and empirically correlates with enhanced Pass@K capability.
A sequential GRPO-ES training strategy successfully integrates GRPO's Pass@1 efficiency with ES's Pass@K coverage gains.
ES performance gains stem from a functionally sparse subset of large-magnitude parameter updates, preventing catastrophic forgetting despite overall parameter drift.
Scaling analysis shows that larger LLMs require a smaller ES population size for effective post-training optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: ES provides a viable, memory-efficient post-training alternative to GRPO that unlocks broader latent LLM reasoning capabilities without triggering catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: The Handoff Tax: Continuing Non-Native Trajectories in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Studying trajectory handoffs between low-capability and high-capability LLM coding agents reveals a 'handoff tax' where full-trajectory model escalation recovers less than half the potential quality gain while driving up costs.
key_points: Model escalation (low-to-high capability) recovers under 50% of the quality gap while incurring significant cost penalties when transferring full trajectories.
Model downshifting (high-to-low capability) provides a favorable cost-quality trade-off for long-running agent tasks.
Interface preferences reverse based on handoff direction: stripping trajectory context improves escalation quality, whereas removing context degrades downshift quality.
Experiments evaluated Claude and GPT model families across different handoff timings, directions, and interfaces (full-trajectory transfer, compaction, and trajectory removal).
summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing how context is passed between cheap and expensive models allows developers to reduce LLM agent execution costs without unnecessarily sacrificing coding accuracy.

papers.title: Rubrics as Visual-Repair Context for Self-Evolving UI-to-Code Generation

summary.tldr: RubSE is a rubric-guided self-evolution framework for UI-to-code generation that uses structured visual-repair contexts to prevent over-broad code edits and visual regression during iterative refinement.
key_points: Identifies visual repair coupling, where localized code edits unintentionally degrade previously correct UI regions via layout and style dependencies.
Generates typed candidate rubrics per iteration, selects a prioritized repair target, and maintains a history of past rubrics to restrict revision scope.
Evaluated across six VLMs and three UI-to-code benchmarks, showing superior performance in final-round and best-round settings compared to naive self-evolution.
Mitigates trajectory collapse by enabling better recovery from visual regressions and allows stronger rubric generators to guide weaker code improver models.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the stability and performance ceiling of iterative VLM code generation by preventing cascading visual errors during automated UI design fixes.

papers.title: Gated Recurrent Transformers: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation

summary.tldr: The Gated Recurrent Transformer uses fixed prelude and coda blocks around a single recurrent core modulated by elementwise update gating to match dense transformer expressivity with significantly fewer parameters.
key_points: Architecture brackets a single core iterated R times with fixed-depth prelude and coda blocks.
Recurrent updates are modulated via a lightweight projection and elementwise update gate conditioned on the hidden state, prelude output, and step-resampled noise.
A 3-layer Gated Recurrent Transformer matches the accuracy of a 12-layer GPT-2 Small baseline under isoFLOPS constraints while outperforming MoR and heavy-tail depth sampling.
Achieves a 2.76 validation loss versus 2.84 for a non-recurrent baseline under isoPARAMS constraints.
At large scale, the architecture yields a 63% parameter reduction and 59% lower peak decoding memory for a 10% increase in compiled generation latency.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large language models to drastically reduce memory usage and parameter count during inference while maintaining quality through recurrent layer reuse.

papers.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution

summary.tldr: WikiSkill is a framework that co-evolves AI agent skills with a persistent wiki-style knowledge base, continuously consolidating execution experience to improve skill synthesis and refinement across iterations.
key_points: Separates raw execution experience, accumulated persistent knowledge (wiki), and executable skills to enable systematic reuse across evolutionary iterations.
Demonstrates that skill evolution complements model scaling: larger models benefit more from evolved skills, while smaller models using skills can surpass larger models without them.
Enables cross-model skill transfer, showing that skills evolved by external models can outperform a model's self-evolved skills.
Ablation studies demonstrate that the persistent knowledge accumulation step within the wiki is critical for effective skill evolution.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling experience into a persistent, evolving knowledge base allows AI agents to continuously build reusable skills that improve performance and transfer effectively across different model architectures and sizes.

papers.title: Performance Foundations of Parallel & Distributed Reasoning Language Models

summary.tldr: This paper presents a compute-centric analysis and parallel computing taxonomy for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) frameworks used to train Reasoning Language Models.
key_points: Evaluates computational demands and compute profiles of post-training algorithmic frameworks including PPO, GRPO, and their variants.
Establishes a taxonomy using the work-depth model to analyze intra- and inter-model parallelism strategies for multi-model RLM pipelines.
Covers core parallelization paradigms such as data, tensor, pipeline, sequence, context, and expert parallelism.
Explores multi-model optimization strategies including disaggregated placement, stage fusion, hybrid parallelism, and asynchronous execution.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides practical system design guidelines for scaling massive, multi-model RLM training pipelines efficiently while reducing hardware costs and runtime bottlenecks.

papers.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that Evolution Strategies (ES) for LLM post-training achieve broader reasoning coverage and avoid entropy collapse compared to GRPO, enabling higher Pass@K performance.
key_points: ES maintains higher population diversity (measured via verifier-projected Jensen-Shannon diversity) and avoids GRPO's entropy collapse, translating directly to higher Pass@K scores while improving Pass@1.
Combining both methods sequentially into a GRPO-ES training pipeline leverages GRPO's strength in Pass@1 optimization alongside ES's superior Pass@K performance gains.

Despite substantial parameter drift across the entire model during ES, task-performance gains are driven by a sparse subset of larger-magnitude updates, preventing catastrophic forgetting on held-out evaluations.
Scaling analysis shows that ES requires smaller population sizes when applied to larger LLMs.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes ES as a complementary, high-coverage post-training paradigm rather than just a memory-efficient GRPO substitute, providing a hybrid training pathway to maximize LLM reasoning capabilities.

papers.title: Disentangling Optimization Scale from Preference Scale in DPO

summary.tldr: A study reveals DPO's beta parameter entangles preference-noise scaling with optimization step size, causing non-monotone policy shifts, and introduces a centered-softplus reformulation to decouple these effects.
key_points: DPO's beta simultaneously dictates the effective inverse preference-noise scale and rescales optimization dynamics, creating a coupling with the effective step size.
At a fixed learning rate, policy deviation from the reference model is non-monotone in beta: it creates a dead zone at small beta, peaks at an intermediate value, and declines at large beta.
Standard DPO loss values are incomparable across different beta parameters, as identical loss curves can exhibit multi-fold differences in KL divergence.
The proposed centered-softplus reformulation is argmin-equivalent to DPO for beta > 0, decouples hyperparameter effects, and yields a linear preference-margin objective as beta approaches 0.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling preference scale from optimization scale reduces hyperparameter sensitivity and simplifies learning-rate tuning during language model alignment.

papers.title: SCIT: Testing Causal Cache Carriers in Latent Chain-of-Thought Models

summary.tldr: SCIT is a causal interchange test that identifies transformer cache components carrying counterfactual computation in latent chain-of-thought models, revealing model- and scale-dependent carrier-regime shifts.
key_points: Introduces the Suffix Cache Interchange Test (SCIT), combining sufficiency/necessity tests, K/V splits, hidden-state controls, and decoded validation to isolate causal mechanisms.
Demonstrates that counterfactual arithmetic in CODI-GPT2 transfers primarily via late-value-suffix cache trajectories rather than hidden states, keys, or single-token triggers.
Shows carrier-regime shifts across scales: arithmetic GPT-2/1B cells rely on latent-tail value/KV transfer, whereas competent 8B models route reasoning through prompt-prefix or full-cache K/V states.
Disproves universal latent-tail claims by demonstrating that carrier mechanisms depend strictly on model competence and task domain.
summary.why_it_matters: SCIT provides a precise, cache-level diagnostic tool to uncover and validate where hidden reasoning occurs inside latent chain-of-thought transformers.

papers.title: Prediction of Prediction (PoP): Inter-Layer Activation Fusion for Single-Pass Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Prediction of Prediction (PoP) detects LLM hallucinations in a single forward pass with under 1.2% latency by fusing intermediate hidden representations across layers.
key_points: Fuses intermediate hidden representations across model depth during a single forward pass to capture layer-transition uncertainty.
Achieves a 75.5% AUROC for factual-correctness classification on the TruthfulQA benchmark using autoregressive transformer backbones.
Requires zero auxiliary generation passes or multi-sample verifications, adding less than 1.2% runtime latency.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables real-time, low-overhead hallucination detection without the high latency and memory costs of multi-sample verification pipelines.

papers.title: TwinKV: A Composable Repair Pass for KV Cache Eviction via Pairwise Key Redundancy

summary.tldr: TwinKV is a training-free, attention-free repair pass that restores lost information in evicted KV caches by swapping redundant retained tokens with evicted orphan tokens.
key_points: A leave-one-out probe demonstrates that attention magnitude does not correlate with a token's causal contribution to model output (Spearman ρ = -0.004).
TwinKV calculates pairwise key redundancy to identify 'orphans' (evicted tokens without duplicates) and 'redundant donors' (retained tokens with duplicates), swapping them under a fixed budget.
Tested across LongBench, LooGLE, RULER, and MMLU-Pro on Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.2-1B at compression ratios 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7.
Improves performance across multiple base eviction policies, though performance gains are minimal at loose compression ratios and ineffective on few-shot classification exemplars.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows existing KV cache eviction algorithms to recover lost context and improve long-context LLM inference efficiency without retraining or altering target cache budgets.

papers.title: Cross-Lingual Alignment Without Joint Training: Do Monolingual Language Models Converge on Universal Representations?

summary.tldr: Monolingual language models trained independently on non-parallel data develop alignable representational geometries that enable functional cross-lingual transfer without joint training.
key_points: Tested strictly monolingual models, including the Goldfish family and independently built models from different labs, to evaluate representational geometry alignment across layers.
Demonstrated that cross-lingual representational alignment increases with model scale, training data scale, and higher linguistic proximity.
Mapped hidden states between models using a single Procrustes rotation fitted on parallel sentences.

Established functional causality by patching a rotated English residual state into a German model during factual cloze tasks, which successfully flipped the German model's output to the donor state's target.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that cross-lingual alignment stems from intrinsic language structure, enabling modular multilingual systems, model merging, and model stitching without computationally expensive joint training.

papers.title: Planting a Latent Variable in Natural-Looking Text: a More Realistic Test of Belief States in LLMs and Their Link to Concept Geometry

summary.tldr: Researchers planted a 8-state ring-shaped Markov latent variable in natural text via SAE steering, showing student LLMs track Bayesian belief states and mirror this geometry.
key_points: Text was generated by an LLM teacher subliminally steered along K=8 sparse autoencoder (SAE) directions following a ring-shaped Markov chain.
A small transformer model trained on the corpus learned to track the Bayesian posterior belief over the planted latent variable.
The student model organized the 8 latent states into a physical ring in activation space, directly matching the Markov chain topology.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides empirical evidence that an LLM's internal feature geometry is directly shaped by the statistical dynamics of latent variables present in its training data.

papers.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance

summary.tldr: SWE-Prime is a two-stage data selection method that filters agent trajectories at the trajectory and segment levels, enabling SFT on just 10% of data while outperforming full-dataset training on SWE-Bench benchmarks.
key_points: Stage one performs trajectory-level screening based on process quality, result quality, and data representativeness to select high-quality successful trajectories.
Stage two conducts segment-level selection by grouping consecutive steps into semantic segments and evaluating them for contribution to the solution, learnability, and risk.
Unselected segments are retained during SFT to preserve contextual continuity, but loss computation is restricted strictly to the selected segments.

Training on a 10% trajectory subset selected by SWE-Prime yields relative performance gains of up to 12.2% on SWE-Bench Pro and 24.2% on SWE-Bench Verified compared to training on the entire resolved dataset.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that masking noisy or redundant steps during loss computation significantly improves software engineering agent performance while reducing SFT data requirements.

papers.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution

summary.tldr: RedEvoAgent is a black-box red-teaming agent that distills cross-case attack trajectories into evolving, human-readable attack skills to jailbreak LLM agents in execution harnesses.
key_points: Targets risks in product-level LLM execution harnesses where jailbreaks cause harmful tool execution and state changes.
Replaces full-trajectory retrieval with distilled, concise attack skills to minimize context overhead and mitigate retrieval bias.
Evolves attack skills adaptively using tool-effectiveness profiling combined with Deciding-Tool Attribution for targeted skill updates.
Incorporates a validation ratchet mechanism that exclusively retains skill modifications that demonstrate performance improvements.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves red-teaming tool efficiency and attack success across different target models and execution harnesses while maintaining context-efficient, interpretable attack strategies.

security.title: Do User-Authored Permission Policies Improve Protection Against AI Agent Overreach?

summary.tldr: A study shows user-authored permission policies using 'allow', 'ask', or 'never' rules block significantly less AI agent overreach than per-action human approval or automated model reviews.
key_points: Evaluated 113 non-software-professional participants across 18-action simulations comparing per-action human-in-the-loop (HITL), automated model review (AUTO), and user-authored consequence policies (POLICY).
POLICY blocked 20.1 percentage points less overreach than HITL (95% CI [-32.1, -8.1]) and 14.5 percentage points less than AUTO (95% CI [-25.8, -3.2]).
POLICY reduced runtime prompts from 18.0 to 10.9, but total intervention time was not reliably lower when rule setup duration was included.
Participants selected 'ask' for 114 of 140 POLICY rules, deferring decisions to runtime where 133 of 148 executed overreach actions were manually approved.
Out of 148 executed overreach actions in POLICY, 15 ran automatically due to 'allow' rules, leading to POLICY having the highest overall approval rate across all overreach actions.
summary.why_it_matters: Pre-authored user access control policies fail to reduce AI agent overreach because users default to case-by-case approvals rather than setting restrictive advance rules.

security.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners

summary.tldr: A benchmark of 170 machine-learning artifacts evaluates static security scanners beyond F1 score by separating judgment accuracy from scanner coverage, analysis completion, and tool redundancy.
key_points: ModelAudit achieved 100% definitive security decisions across 135 labeled artifact families, compared to Fickling at 81.5% (110) and ModelScan at 49.6% (67).
ModelScan achieved 100% precision, recall, and F1 on the subset of artifacts where it made a definitive judgment, but failed to complete analysis on 48 malicious families.
ModelAudit and Fickling successfully generated accurate detections for all 48 malicious families that caused ModelScan analysis failures.
Fickling provided no unique true-positive family detections beyond the combined detections of ModelAudit and ModelScan.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating AI security scanners purely on traditional F1 scores hides analysis completion failures, making multi-metric benchmarks necessary to assess real-world scanner reliability and redundancy.

security.title: When Context Gets Root: Privilege Escalation in LLM Harnesses

summary.tldr: Researchers identified instruction privilege escalation, a vulnerability where LLM agent harnesses inadvertently promote low-level untrusted context to higher-privilege instruction levels during context construction.
key_points: Instruction privilege escalation occurs when an agent harness places low-level malicious content into context spaces that the model treats as high-privilege instructions.
Attacks evaluated across six coding-agent harnesses achieved 13 distinct objectives covering confidentiality, integrity, availability, and remote code execution.
The attack succeeded 100% of the time under both unrestricted action execution (6/6 harnesses) and automatic permission review modes (3/3 harnesses).
Vulnerabilities were successfully reproduced using persistent goals, multi-agent mechanisms, and scheduled tasks provided by the harnesses.
summary.why_it_matters: Model-side instruction hierarchy defenses can be completely bypassed if the surrounding agent harness mismanages context levels during execution.

security.title: SPA: Securing Persistent LLM Agents Across Queries with Plan-First Information-Flow Control

summary.tldr: SPA is a plan-first architecture that uses a declarative domain-specific language and dual-lattice information-flow control to secure persistent LLM agents against cross-query data flow and control attacks.
key_points: Invokes the planner once per query to generate an executable plan in a declarative domain-specific language.
Applies dual-lattice information-flow control (IFC) to track confidentiality and integrity across explicit data flows and control dependencies.
Stores execution results as labeled artifacts, exposing only semantic metadata during subsequent planning to prevent untrusted payloads from re-entering the planner.
Introduces AgentDojo-MQ, a multi-query benchmark extension designed to measure secure state reuse and delayed security attacks.
Reduces 'tool_knowledge' attack success to 0% on AgentDojo and 0.2% on AgentDojo-MQ, though strict integrity enforcement reveals a security-utility tradeoff.
summary.why_it_matters: SPA demonstrates that combining single-pass declarative planning with label-preserving state persistence can effectively prevent indirect prompt injection and control-flow hijacking in multi-query LLM agents.

security.title: Safety Does Not Compose: Non-Decaying Loop State for Autonomous LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that trajectory-scoped safeguards fail against multi-iteration agent attacks, and propose LoopHarness, a loop-level framework using non-decaying state to bound unauthorized irreversible actions independent of horizon length.
key_points: Trajectory-scoped safety monitors perform no better than random guessing (true-positive rate equals false-positive rate) when attack evidence is fragmented across iterations.
Carrying a geometrically decaying risk score is ineffective because an adversary only needs to wait a constant cooling-off period regardless of horizon length N.
LoopHarness maintains persistent, non-decaying state to bound expected unauthorized irreversible actions to B + m - 1 + m/δ_M, a constant relative to horizon N.
The bound's B + m - 1 component relies on a model-free rule that remains resilient even against a fully colluding verifier.
Evaluation includes an outer-state attack suite on Agent-SafetyBench, module ablations, and adaptive white-box red-teaming.
summary.why_it_matters: Autonomous LLM agents operating in multi-step loops require persistent safety state across iterations, as traditional single-trajectory guards cannot detect distributed adversarial attacks.

security.title: The Framing Gap: Indirect Prompt-Injection Exfiltration Defeats Surface-Level Defenses in Tool-Using Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers identify the framing gap in tool-using LLM agents, where reframing data exfiltration as legitimate operations increases gpt-4o secret leaks from 0% to 100% despite surface-level prompt injection defenses.
key_points: Reframing exfiltration as integrity signatures, config fields, or look-alike hosts bypasses alignment, driving gpt-4o attack success from 0% to 100%.
Ablations show the failure stems from instruction/data confusion rather than defeated alignment policies, as removing confidentiality rules leaves base attacks at 0%.
Payload-blind architectural defenses, specifically destination allow-lists and planner/reader capability isolation, successfully reduced exfiltration rates to 0%.
Existing defenses like SecAlign fine-tuning (32.5%), channel separation (38.8%), and output-normalizing guards (defeated 100% by ROT13) fail to prevent the attack.
summary.why_it_matters: Robust agent security cannot rely on the acting model detecting attacks, requiring architectural controls like destination allow-lists and capability isolation instead.

security.title: The Guard That Cried Wolf: How Scary Words Make Agent Guardrails Refuse Legitimate Actions

summary.tldr: Researchers created Cautious Bench, a policy-grounded benchmark revealing that agent guardrails suffer from a name-superstition effect, over-refusing safe actions when presented with scary-looking object names.
key_points: Cautious Bench evaluates guardrail over-safety by codesigning sample actions and labels with explicit authorization policies, using a build-time gate to certify label correctness.
The benchmark contains 756 decidable benign/twin pairs evaluated across three object-name types (2,268 total measured pairs), plus 40 undecidable pairs.
Evaluation of six guardrails spanning five design architectures showed consistent over-refusal of authorized actions driven solely by scary object names rather than authorization context.
summary.why_it_matters: Guardrails that rely on surface-level keyword superstition rather than contextual policy logic block legitimate automated deployments by refusing authorized operations.

security.title: PLCBench: Can Autonomous LLM Agents Turn PLC Access into Sustained Physical Impact?

summary.tldr: PLCBench is the first hardware-in-the-loop benchmark designed to evaluate whether tool-using LLM agents can exploit network-reachable commercial PLCs to cause sustained physical impact.
key_points: Evaluates five LLM agent families across 240 real-PLC episodes combining four commercial PLCs with four closed-loop workloads.
Achieved sustained physical impact objectives in 31.3% (75/240) of overall episodes, with 98 failing before a valid native read and 62 failing after a process-linked write.
Utilizes a deterministic evaluator with six hidden diagnostic flags tracking native interaction, process-linked manipulation, and sustained physical impact.
Demonstrates that richer process observation increases the conditional objective attainment rate after a process-linked write from 44.2% to 64.0%.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that evaluating cyber attacks purely at the software exploitation or write-access level mischaracterizes physical risk, establishing a realistic baseline for ICS defenses.

security.title: Daydreaming: Stealing Hidden Agent Skills through Black-Box Task Interaction

summary.tldr: Daydreaming is a novel execution-only attack that functionally steals multi-file LLM agent skills using adaptive task interactions under strict black-box output constraints.
key_points: Operates at the Output threat level where the attacker only observes final responses and returned files, bypassing direct disclosure defenses.
Uses attacker-controlled shadow agents and local execution checks to adaptively generate tasks, test specific behaviors, and reconstruct skill files.
Achieves 86.8% capability recovery of original skills across 7 skills and 4 victim models, outperforming SigLeak by nearly 4x.
Requires a median of only 32 victim calls per skill to produce fully installable reconstructed skills.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that hosted LLM agent services cannot rely on hidden skill files and prompt-filtering defenses to protect proprietary intellectual property from functional theft.

security.title: Five Primitives for Governing Autonomous AI Agents at Runtime

summary.tldr: A runtime governance framework introduces five structural primitives to discover, identify, govern, attest, and secure the supply chain for ephemeral, model-driven autonomous AI agents.
key_points: Identifies three enterprise control failures: ephemeral agent principals, unprogrammed model-selected actions, and unprovisioned agent populations.
Derives five essential runtime primitives: discovery, identity, governance, attestation, and supply chain.
Enforces policy via a request-path mediation point, per-tenant action vocabularies, sidecar identity workloads, and a third-party-verifiable hash-linked signed ledger.
Incurs concrete trade-offs including request-path latency, sidecar overhead, and fail-closed behavior that converts availability incidents into access denials.
Implements four primitives in private pilots and maintains one primitive as separate unintegrated tooling.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a concrete runtime architecture for enforcing policy and cryptographically auditing unpredictable autonomous agent actions before they execute.

security.title: Beyond Vector Hiding: Breaking and Mitigating Shared-Direction Weight Obfuscation in TEE-Offloaded Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers broke ArrowCloak's TEE weight obfuscation scheme using two attacks, SpectralLeak and LatticeLeak, and proposed a new defense called ButterflyCloak.
key_points: ArrowCloak's reuse of scalar multiples of a hidden direction across weight vectors creates a rank-one relation in the accelerator-visible matrix.
SpectralLeak targets the real-valued scheme, achieving surrogates with 87.98% mean accuracy compared to 89.85% for victims across 12 task settings.
LatticeLeak targets the modular (mod-Q) scheme by exploiting the hidden lattice to exactly reconstruct every fixed-point parameter for BERT-Base and GPT2-Base without queries, labels, or fine-tuning.
ButterflyCloak is proposed as a replacement defense, using a keyed maximal-rank butterfly mask to eliminate shared-direction reuse while maintaining fast TEE correction.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that shared rank-one components in model obfuscation allow untrusted accelerators to fully reconstruct protected LLM weights without active querying.

security.title: The Latent Diagnostic Taxonomy: A Framework for Constructing Classifiers and Diagnosing Their Decisions, Applied to Prompt Injection Detection

summary.tldr: The Latent Diagnostic Taxonomy framework optimizes classifier embedding dimensionality, isolates latent support vectors, and uses token-level perturbation analysis to diagnose brittleness and guide safety treatments for prompt injection detectors.
key_points: Identifies influential prompts by isolating a latent support vector subset comprising approximately 29% of the total training examples.
Reveals that roughly 77% of confident classifier decisions on a public prompt injection dataset are brittle to single-token removals.
Categorizes non-robust decisions into two distinct failure patterns: confidence calibration failure and exploitable shortcuts.
Establishes a diagnostic taxonomy that routes input prompts into four treatment zones: Safely rely, Heuristic Bias, Heuristic Override, and Insufficient Context.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a practical diagnostic pipeline to identify hidden failure modes in prompt injection safeguards and determine when model predictions can be trusted.

security.title: SILK: Closing the Time-of-Check-to-Time-of-Use Gap in RoT-Protected AI Systems

summary.tldr: SILK closes the TOCTOU gap in RoT-protected AI systems by repurposing quantized-weight LSBs as secret-keyed integrity bits and verifying weight streams with commit gating at the final pre-compute boundary.
key_points: Repurposes LSBs of quantized weights as secret-keyed integrity bits and chains byte dependencies to detect post-verification tampering across DRAM, DMA, and interconnect paths.
Uses a lightweight streaming checker with commit gating to recompute checks without separate authentication tags, causing forgery probability to drop exponentially under a secure PRF.
Demonstrates zero missed detections across a functional attack suite, with INT8 quality impact under 0.76 pp for evaluated CNNs and 0.17 perplexity across eight LLMs.
FPGA synthesis on a Xilinx ZCU102 achieves 756 MB/s at 1.00% of the area cost of a Caliptra 2.x RoT, or 678 MB/s at 6.15% RoT cost for a 2^-128 forgery bound.
summary.why_it_matters: SILK protects neural network weights against physical and interconnect tampering between load-time authentication and execution without needing separate storage tags or substantial hardware overhead.

summary.tldr: Microsoft's August 2026 security updates introduce AI agent containment guidelines, expanded Defender Experts MDR data coverage, elevated Purview auto-labeling limits, and new Entra and Intune management capabilities.
key_points: Microsoft Defender Experts MDR P2 extends 24/7 threat detection and response to third-party data sources ingested via Microsoft Sentinel, including AWS, Okta, and Palo Alto Networks.
Microsoft Purview auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive files increased fivefold, from 100,000 to 500,000 files per day, to accelerate Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness.
Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance adds continuous configuration drift reports with timestamped property details and cross-tenant delegated administration to mitigate shadow-tenant risk.

Microsoft Intune introduces Windows Autopilot device association for pre-enrollment customization and Windows Unattended Support with Remote Sign-In featuring built-in auditing and role-based permissions.
Microsoft Security Exposure Management launched 'Secure Now' guidance to establish agentic containment controls that constrain unapproved autonomous AI agent actions.
summary.why_it_matters: These updates allow enterprise security teams to secure autonomous AI agent workflows, scale data loss prevention controls for Copilot deployments, and centralize threat response across multi-cloud and third-party telemetry.

security.title: What Zero Trust Can Teach Us About AI Watermarks

summary.tldr: Anthropic is implementing AI text watermarking to comply with EU AI Act transparency rules, highlighting the growing technical difficulty of distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written content.
key_points: Anthropic is adding watermarks to AI-generated text specifically to meet the compliance mandates of the EU AI Act's transparency rules.
Differentiating between AI-generated and human-authored text is becoming increasingly difficult as model outputs advance.
summary.why_it_matters: Compliance-driven measures like text watermarking highlight the broader industry challenge of establishing content provenance without disrupting the utility of AI as a productivity tool.

infra.title: Deploy an Open Model from Checkpoint to Inference in Two Commands with NVIDIA TensorRT Model Connect

summary.tldr: NVIDIA released TensorRT Model Connect, an open collection of reference implementations designed to simplify running supported open AI models with native C++ using TensorRT.
key_points: Provides reference code to streamline model-specific conversion, preprocessing, post-processing, and runtime setup.
Enables integration of open AI models directly into native C++ applications using NVIDIA TensorRT.
summary.why_it_matters: It reduces the manual engineering effort required to convert, process, and deploy open AI model checkpoints into high-performance C++ inference pipelines.

infra.title: Spreading the load: How Salesforce met Multi-AZ HA with SageMaker Inference Components

summary.tldr: Salesforce used Amazon SageMaker's SchedulingConfig parameter in the CreateInferenceComponent API to achieve Multi-AZ high availability while preserving an 8x infrastructure cost reduction.
key_points: Default SageMaker Inference Component (IC) placement optimizes operations independently, risking uneven model copy distribution across Availability Zones (AZs) and instances.
The SchedulingConfig parameter introduces AvailabilityZoneBalance to control cross-AZ copy distribution via EnforcementMode and MaxImbalance parameters.
PlacementStrategy offers SPREAD to distribute copies across maximum instances for fault isolation or BINPACK to maximize compute utilization efficiency within an AZ.
Scaling operations (CopyCount adjustments) automatically preserve configured AZ balance by symmetrically adding or removing copies across zones.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows enterprise workloads to combine the cost savings of co-hosting multiple models on shared GPUs with strict Multi-AZ compliance and fault isolation requirements.

infra.title: Core PyTorch Sessions at PyTorch Conference North America 2026

summary.tldr: PyTorch Conference NA 2026 announced core technical sessions covering C++ ABI stability tools, agentic CI infrastructure, and out-of-tree backend compatibility frameworks.
key_points: Out-of-tree backend releases use `instantiate_device_type_tests` and dynamic skipping to reuse over 580K community test cases out of the box.
The Cross-Repository CI Relay (CRCR) implements a four-tier trust model to forward PyTorch PR events downstream, reducing NPU and RISC-V breakage detection from days to minutes.
Meta integrated Claude into PyTorch infrastructure via @claude triggers, AWS Bedrock/OIDC, and two-stage GitHub Actions to automate PR reviews, issue triage, and autorevert investigations.
PyTorch ecosystem engineering is updating C++ extension tooling to audit and inventory unstable API usage, advancing a binary-compatible stable C ABI interface.
summary.why_it_matters: These infrastructure developments reduce upstream breakage and shorten out-of-tree hardware backend release cycles to under 30 days while maintaining binary compatibility.

infra.title: Introducing OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock for in-country inferencing in India

summary.tldr: Amazon Bedrock now supports OpenAI GPT-5.6 Terra and Luna models in India via local geographic cross-Region inference between the Mumbai and Hyderabad AWS Regions.
key_points: Supports OpenAI GPT-5.6 Terra (in.openai.gpt-5.6-terra) and Luna (in.openai.gpt-5.6-luna) models featuring a 1-million-token context window for text and image inputs.
India geographic cross-Region inference strictly routes workloads between ap-south-1 (Mumbai) and ap-south-2 (Hyderabad) to meet local data residency requirements.
Requests can be submitted using the OpenAI Responses API, OpenAI Chat Completions API, or the Amazon Bedrock Converse API via the bedrock-runtime endpoint.
Uses a Zero Data Retention (ZDR) model by default, with encrypted transit between India Regions, though content flagged by automated abuse-detection classifiers is retained for offline review.
Billing, CloudWatch monitoring, CloudTrail logs, and quotas are recorded exclusively within the source Region.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations with strict Indian data sovereignty regulations in healthcare, finance, and the public sector can now scale deployment of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 models without data leaving the country.

summary.tldr: Anthropic released a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard, a model-agnostic specification that lets AI agents safely interface with physical laboratory and manufacturing equipment.
key_points: Reduces physical hardware integration times from weeks to hours or minutes using a standardized driver layer.
Uses simple read and write primitives to operate devices like microscopes, liquid handlers, and robotic arms via programmable interfaces.
Integrates with standard protocols like the Model Context Protocol to make hardware discoverable across networks to any agent harness.
Embeds natural language tags and safety limits directly into automatically generated reference files to inform agents of physical constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes an open framework for AI agents to autonomously orchestrate, monitor, and recover multi-device physical workflows without requiring custom integration code for every tool.

summary.tldr: Anthropic is expanding its scientific support by providing 10,000 discounted or free Claude Team Plan seats and extending its AI for Science grant program to non-biological research fields.
key_points: The new Claude team plan for scientists offers 10,000 seats featuring free standard tiers and $15/month premium tiers with 5x usage limits for verified academic or non-profit principal investigators.
The AI for Science program provides up to $50,000 in credits per project for compute-heavy research, expanding beyond biology into fields like chemistry and mathematics.
Biology and chemistry researchers remain restricted to Opus-class models, as Claude Fable models block professional biology and drug development queries due to dual-use risks.
Anthropic is partnering with the US government to establish a controlled access program allowing life sciences professionals to use Mythos-class models.
summary.why_it_matters: The expanded plan lowers barriers to advanced compute and LLM integration for academic researchers while maintaining explicit safety restrictions on dual-use biological queries.

vendors.title: Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode

summary.tldr: Security researcher Johann Rehberger bypassed Claude Code Opus 5's default auto mode with an 80% success rate using a prompt injection technique that trickles in local file execution via a extracted zip archive.
key_points: The attack tricks Claude Code into downloading and uncompressing a zip file, then executing code that imports base64, which inadvertently triggers a local struct.py file extracted from the archive.
Auto mode's classifier allowed the creation of the malware process but subsequently blocked Claude's own attempt to execute a cleanup command after detecting the compromise.
The security vulnerability demonstrates that auto mode classifiers can act as a failure mode by preventing automated agent cleanup actions.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying on auto mode classifiers for prompt injection defense is insufficient, necessitating strict containerization, VM sandboxing, egress restrictions, and credential isolation for unattended agents.

vendors.title: Training and Finetuning Multi-Vector Embedding Models with Sentence Transformers

summary.tldr: The Sentence Transformers library does not currently support training or fine-tuning multi-vector embedding models.
key_points: Sentence Transformers currently lacks implementation and support for multi-vector encoder training pipelines.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers requiring multi-vector representations must use alternative libraries or custom implementations until Sentence Transformers adds native support.
